spec.footprint: fcjamma:JAMMA_Edge_56 (J1): the board's own 56-position JAMMA card edge. 54 gold-finger pads of type 'connect': 27 on F.Cu ('1'-'28' without '7') and 27 on B.Cu ('A'-'f' without 'H'). Position 7/H is the key slot. No part is placed. The footprint holds the pads, the mask opening, three keep-out rule areas, the courtyard, fab and silk; the board generator draws the tongue, key slot and shoulder on Edge.Cuts.
spec.summary:
Origin (0,0) is where the board tip line (the tongue end on Edge.Cuts) crosses the centre line of finger 1 and A. +X runs toward finger 28/f. The fingers and the board lie at negative Y. Seen from the parts side, the tip is at the bottom and finger 1 is on the left. This matches JST's 'PC board layout (viewed from component side)' and mech/floorplan.py.

All 54 pads are KiCad pad type 'connect', shape rect, 2.30 x 8.80 mm, centred at Y = -5.6. Copper runs from 1.2 to 10.0 mm from the tip. X = 3.96 * index, so pad 1/A is at 0 and pad 28/f at 106.92. Each B.Cu pad sits at the same X as its F.Cu partner (A behind 1 ... f behind 28). Layers are F.Cu+F.Mask or B.Cu+B.Mask, with no paste and no drill.

Inside the footprint:
- A full-band mask opening on F.Mask and B.Mask from (-4.24, 0.5) to (111.16, -10.5).
- Three keep-out rule areas on F.Cu+B.Cu: the tip strip from 0 to -1.2 (no copper at all); the contact band from -1.2 to -9.0 (no tracks, vias or pour); the finger roots from -9.0 to -11.0 (no vias or pour).
- Courtyard on F.CrtYd and B.CrtYd out to Y = -12.0.
- A fab outline of the tongue.
- Silk labels at Y = -13.4.
- attr exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom allow_soldermask_bridges.

The board generator draws on Edge.Cuts: the tongue (114.4 wide, X -3.74 to +110.66, 0.5 x 45 deg corners), the key slot (centre X 23.76, 3.0 wide, 11.5 deep, C0.5 mouth, R0.5 bottom) and the shoulder at Y = -12.0. It also sets the stackup flag (edge_connector bevelled).

Every value traces to the JST GEC drawing, the Hirose CR7E-30DB drawing, the Sullins catalogue and JLCPCB's gold-finger and capability pages, all re-read on 2026-11-15. The one exception is the Hirose CR7 catalogue (unreachable; its values come only from the research notes).

I checked the syntax and the DRC behaviour with a KiCad 10.0.8 probe board in the scratchpad. The full spec gives a clean DRC. Without allow_soldermask_bridges, DRC reports 199 mask-bridge errors.

One correction to the notes: the Hirose contact point is 5.3 +/- 0.4 mm from the tip of a fully seated board, not 3.2. The footprint does not change.

Nothing in the repository was edited.

spec.other_geometry:
All values are in mm, in the footprint frame: origin on the tip line at the finger-1/A centre, +X toward 28/f, Y downward, board at Y < 0. All 54 pads are type 'connect'.

A. Items inside fcjamma:JAMMA_Edge_56
1. Mask opening. fp_rect (start -4.24 0.5) (end 111.16 -10.5), stroke width 0, fill yes, layer F.Mask, and the same rect on B.Mask. No other mask, paste or Edge.Cuts items.
2. Rule areas. Each is a zone on (layers "F.Cu" "B.Cu") with footprints allowed:
   - K1 tip strip: (-4.24,0.5) (111.16,0.5) (111.16,-1.2) (-4.24,-1.2). Tracks, vias, pads and copperpour not_allowed.
   - K2 contact band: (-4.24,-1.2) (111.16,-1.2) (111.16,-9.0) (-4.24,-9.0). Tracks, vias and copperpour not_allowed; pads allowed.

verdicts.evidence: JST p.295, which I downloaded again (/tmp/claude-0/fp-spec/jamma-verify/jst_gec.pdf) and rendered at 150 and 600 dpi. The title reads 'PC board layout (viewed from component side)'. 'Circuit No.1' is the leftmost finger and 'Circuit No.28' the rightmost. At 600 dpi the fingers run from y=1931 down to a continuous bottom line at y=2056; the key groove at position 7 breaks that line, so the bottom line is the tip. The 'C0.5' leader points at the tongue's lower right corner, and the cross-section shows the rounded edge at the bottom. floorplan.py has 'FINGER1_X = TONGUE_X0 + 3.74' with TONGUE_X0 = (220-114.4)/2 = 52.8, giving 56.54, and 'y = 0 is the tip of the fingers'. KiCad's DEC_double_long uses the same frame: pads sit at negative Y above a tip at Y about 0 ((at 127.7874 -7.6501) (size 2.032 14.3002), so the pad spans -14.8 to -0.5). Note for the generator: floorplan y points up and KiCad Y points down, so the sign flips.

I generated the names myself from the symbols.py rules ('comp = [n for n in range(1, 29) if n != 7]', 'sold = [c for c in "ABCDEFHJKLMNPRSTUVWXYZabcdef" if c != "H"]'). They equal the 54 pin numbers of JAMMA56 in kicad/fcjamma.kicad_sym and the 54 J1 rows of out/netlist_by_part.csv. GND is 1,2,14,27,28,A,B,e,f; +5V_IN is 3,4,C,D; (NC) is 5,6,11,E,F,M. Sullins prints '(LETTERS G, I, O & Q NOT USED)'. The Hirose catalogue, which I re-read, says 'following 8 alphabetic characters are not used. G. I, O, Q, g, i, o, q'. In my own pcbnew 10.0.8 test, a footprint whose only pad is 'a' returns FindPadByNumber('a') = pad and FindPadByNumber('A') = None, so pad names are case-sensitive.

In JST's lower view (my 600 dpi crops), 'Circuit No.A' is the leftmost finger and carries the same '3.84 +0/-0.1' and '106.92 ±0.05' dimensions as No.1. 'Circuit No.H Mis-insertion preventive key groove' is at position 7 and 'Circuit No.F' (meaning f) is at the right end. The lower view is the upper view mirrored about the horizontal axis (tip at its top), so X is preserved. KiCad's DEC_double_long has pad AA1 (F.Cu F.Mask) and AA2 (B.Cu B.Mask) at the same (at 127.7874 -7.6501). The Hirose drawing ADC-016737-72-02 lists contact numbers as '1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 ... / A B C D E F H J K ...'.

JST: '3.96 ±0.05(.156 ±.002)' and '106.92 ±0.05(4.209 ±.002)'. My row scan of the upper view found 28 finger outlines from x=1317 to x=2656 at 600 dpi, i.e. 48.37 px per pitch. The Hirose CR7 catalogue (re-read, p.A11) gives 'A±0.08' with A = 106.98 for 56 contacts, and '3.96±0.05'. Sullins: '28/56 4.212 ... 106.98' with 'A±0.20'. 27 x 3.96 = 106.92 lies inside 106.87-106.97 (JST), 106.90-107.06 (Hirose) and 106.78-107.18 (Sullins). 27 x 3.9624 = 106.985 exceeds JST's 106.97.

JST lower view: '2.3 ±0.035(.091±.001)'. Upper view: '2.3 ±0.35 (.091 ±.001)'. In both views my scans put the extension lines at x of about 1463 and 1495 px. Those are finger 4's two edges (1462-1465 and 1493-1495), at 12.2 px/mm, so the dimension is a finger width, not a gap. Hirose catalogue (re-read): '2.3±0.1', with its extension lines on one finger. Hirose 30-pole drawing: '( 2 )(接触巾)', whose extension lines are 95 px apart = 2.0 mm at 2:1. Gap 3.96 - 2.30 = 1.66.

I re-downloaded the JLCPCB figure copper-setback-definition.png. It reads '1.6 mm | 30 ± 5° | Approx. 1.13 mm' and '1.6 mm | 45 ± 5° | Approx. 0.74 mm', plus '1) A thicker board requires a longer copper setback.' JST draws the fingers from the tip line to y=1931: 124 px = 10.15 mm at the pitch scale. One caveat on the spec's reading: the '10.0(.394)' dimension at x=851 has its upper arrowhead on the notch-bottom line (y=1911), while the finger-top extension line (y=1931) merely ends on that dimension line. So the drawing is ambiguous about what '10.0' measures. The drawn length still supports a 10.0 root, and 1.2-10.0 is a sound inference.

I scanned the Hirose CR7E-30DB section at 1200 dpi. The two extension lines of '5.3±0.4(接点位置)' are at y=1574 and y=2076: 502 px = 5.31 mm at 2:1. The lower line coincides with the slot bottom (a thick line at 2065-2087). The housing top face (1261-1284) is 803.5 px = 8.50 mm above the slot bottom and 3.19 mm above the upper line. The front view's '( 8.5 )(基板挿入深さ)' runs from the top face to the dashed slot bottom. So the contact is 5.3±0.4 mm from a seated board tip, and the notes' 3.2 is the distance from the housing face. The catalogue's single 3.96 mm figure shows '8.5' for every size, but its table gives F = 11.1 for 56 contacts against 9 for 30, so the 56-pole section is not proven identical. The finger (1.2-10.0) covers any plausible position.

Non-Plated Slots 1.0mm' and 'Rectangular holes and slots without rounded corners are not supported.' README chapter 8: '挿入部品は金フィンガーから 5 mm 以上、ほかの基板端から 2.5 mm 以上離す' and '金フィンガーは耐熱テープで覆い、はんだやフラックスを付けない'. -15.0 = -10.0 - 5 is right. My probe loaded the F.Fab polyline without problems. Cosmetic: the Fab outline draws the slot bottom square, whereas Edge.Cuts has R0.5.

The rule 'end point at Y <= -9.0 - w/2' alone also allows ends beyond the pad root (Y < -10.0), and such a track does not connect. My probe shows that a 2.0 mm track ending exactly at -10.0 is connected and passes K2. The sentence 'front/back pairs are tied' would also tie finger 14 (GND) to R, which is J_SERVICE in the netlist. The 3 A rating ('Current rating: 3A AC, DC') and S8 #9 are quoted correctly.
verdicts.correction: A track enters a finger only from its root, with -10.0 <= y_end <= -9.0 - w/2. The end must lie on the pad, and its cap must stay out of K2. That limits a straight entry to w <= 2.0 mm, and a 2.0 mm track must end exactly at -10.0. Vias go at y <= -11.0 - r; the -11.5 guideline suits vias up to 1.0 mm. Tie front to back only for same-net pairs: 1/A and 2/B (GND), 3/C and 4/D (+5V_IN), 27/e and 28/f (GND). Finger 14 (GND) is backed by R (J_SERVICE) and must not be tied. No sideways track may run inside the mask opening (Y > -10.5). NC fingers 5, 6, 11, E, F and M stay unrouted.

verdicts.evidence: I re-read the primary catalogue. The plain URL returns 404, but dtsheet.com/model/1263367 links 'Open as PDF' to https://s1.dtsheet.com/store/data/002648525.pdf?key=d5d0a71015d5aed7a7c114bf59f02bf7&r=1, which downloaded (6 pages, alldatasheet copy, created 2004-01-26; saved as /tmp/claude-0/fp-spec/jamma-verify/hirose_cr7_cat.pdf). Page A11, 'PCB Dimensions 3.96 pitch', shows '2.3±0.1', '3.96±0.05', 'A±0.08', 'B' with tolerance 0/-0.2, '11 +0.5/0', '10', '1 +0.1/0', '2.5 +0.1/0', 'C0.5' at the tip faces, the tongue corners and both mouths, '1.6±0.15', and 'Mis-insertion preventive key (Recommended)'. The table gives 56: 'A 106.98' and 'B 114.80'. The wide groove is centred on a contact line. The page also shows a narrow between-contacts groove 1 +0.1/0 by 10, which JAMMA does not need.

In KiCad 10.0.8, pcbnew.FromMM(3*3.96) = 11879999 nm (it truncates; 3*3.96 = 11.879999999999999), so pcbnew writes 11.879999. The project's writer (sexpr.fmt, f"{v:.6f}" then rstrip) already prints '11.88'. Rounding to 0.001 matters only for pcbnew-API-built boards.

JLCPCB capabilities, re-fetched: '③ Dimension tolerance for routed board edges: ±0.2 mm (regular precision); ±0.1 mm (high precision)' and '④ Minimum dimension 50*50mm for high precision, and at least 3 tooling holes with minimum 1.5mm diameter on different corners.' So 114.5±0.1 = 114.4-114.6, which lies inside JST's range.

verification.pad_table_check:
All 54 pads are correct.
- Names: no duplicates. I generated the names independently from symbols.py's comp/sold rules. The set equals the 54 JAMMA56 pin numbers in kicad/fcjamma.kicad_sym and the 54 J1 rows of out/netlist_by_part.csv. Lower-case a-f are distinct from A-F, and pcbnew pad lookup is case-sensitive.
- Coordinates: in the stated frame (origin on the tip line at the 1/A centre, +X toward 28/f, board at -Y), every pad has x = 3.96 x position index. Letters are indexed in ABCDEFHJKLMNPRSTUVWXYZabcdef, so each letter has the same x as its number. 1/A is at 0 and 28/f at 106.92. Index 6 (7/H) is empty.
- Geometry: every pad has y = -5.6 and is a 2.3 x 8.8 rect, so copper runs from -1.2 to -10.0. Drill is 0.
- Layers: numbers on F.Cu F.Mask, letters on B.Cu B.Mask, no paste.
- Pitch and spacing: the pitch is 3.96 and the front and back rows are coincident in XY. The edge-to-edge gap between neighbours is 1.66, and 5.62 across the key.
- JLCPCB limits: there are no holes, so PTH annular ring and drill limits do not apply. 1.66 is at least the 0.15 SMD pad-to-pad minimum. Copper is 1.20 from the tip, 1.31 from the slot side, 1.42 from the mouth chamfer and 2.59 from the tongue sides, all at least 0.2 from a routed edge. The band has no mask webs, so the 0.10 soldermask-bridge minimum does not apply.
- KiCad 10.0.8 probe, from my own boards built from this table, with the outline and rule areas, run through kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones:
  - the spec as written: 0 errors;
  - without allow_soldermask_bridges: 199 solder_mask_bridge;
  - with K1 moved to -1.5: 54 items_not_allowed.
missing: Source S4 needs updating: the Hirose CR7 catalogue can be fetched. dtsheet.com/model/1263367 has an 'Open as PDF' link with a key parameter (https://s1.dtsheet.com/store/data/002648525.pdf?key=d5d0a71015d5aed7a7c114bf59f02bf7&r=1). Its page A11 confirms every Hirose value the spec took from the notes, so open question 2 is resolved. The brief asked for the Hirose drawings to be re-read; the spec skipped this one.

Routing rule: the track end point needs both bounds, -10.0 <= y_end <= -9.0 - w/2, which also caps a straight entry at w <= 2.0 mm. Only same-net front/back pairs may be tied; 14 (GND) is backed by R (J_SERVICE). See the routing correction.

Exposed copper inside the mask opening: track stubs between the finger roots (-10.0) and the mask edge (-10.5) are bare ENIG. JLCPCB requires 'Minimum trace width/clearance: 0.25/0.25mm, when traces are NOT covered by solder mask' and 'Keep at least 0.09 mm clearance between soldermask openings and neighboring traces'. The spec should forbid sideways runs at Y > -10.5. K3 allows tracks there and only the clearance check would catch one.

The README rule 'THT parts at least 5 mm from the gold fingers' (Y <= -15.0) has only an optional Cmts.User line; nothing enforces it. Add a named rule area plus a custom DRC rule, or a generator check, that rejects THT pads above Y = -15.0 relative to J1.

tools/check_footprints.py would not catch the errors that matter for this footprint. It compares only the exclude_from_pos_files and exclude_from_bom attributes and the keep-out bounding boxes. expected.json for JAMMA_Edge_56 should also check allow_soldermask_bridges (pcbnew fp.AllowSolderMaskBridges()), each keep-out's flags and layers (GetDoNotAllowTracks/Vias/Pads/ZoneFills), the F.Mask and B.Mask band rectangles, and the two courtyards.

No automated check ties J1 to the outline. The footprint has no Edge.Cuts, so the board generator should verify that J1 sits at (FINGER1_X, tip) with rotation 0 on F.Cu, and that the tongue, key slot and shoulder match the spec (floorplan outline_path still lacks the slot's C0.5 mouth and R0.5 bottom).

Contact position is still unverified for the 56-pole parts. The Hirose catalogue gives F = 11.1 for the 56-pole against 9 for the 30-pole drawing used. The JST GEC and Sullins contact points and the JST insertion depth are not published. The 1.2 setback is safe only if the contact lands more than about 1.5 mm from the seated tip; check with a real cabinet harness.

JST drawing ambiguity, for the record: the '10.0(.394)' dimension's upper arrowhead (at x=851, 600 dpi) touches the notch-bottom line rather than the finger-top line. The 10.0 finger root rests on the drawn length (10.15 mm), not on an unambiguous dimension.

Minor: footprint_out.py hard-codes the Reference and Value font at 1.0/0.15, exactly JLCPCB's minimum text height and line width. The JST key GEC-PK2 (drawn 2.3/1.6) is not cited in key_slot, though it fits the 3.0 slot. The F.Fab slot bottom is square while Edge.Cuts has R0.5.

spec.summary:
J8 = WingTAT ED60BGFBK (JLCPCB/LCSC C5173310), checked against the maker drawing 'EDxxxBGFBK' Rev A (S1). It is a 60-way (2 x 30) card-edge slot with 2.54 +-0.05 pitch and rows 5.08 +-0.05 apart. The two rows are not staggered. Straight through-hole tails, 0.65 x 0.40 mm, 3.80 mm below the seating plane. Recommended PCB hole is Ø1.00 +-0.15 (the second 'Recommended Card Layout' view on the drawing is really the PCB hole pattern). Body is 82.49 x 9.25 mm and 15.60 mm high. Card slot is 79.04 x 2.00 mm, 9.00 deep. There are no pegs, posts or non-plated holes: the body stands on two end legs whose outer faces are 80.74 apart. Recommended card thickness is 1.57 +-0.15. The drawing has no pin numbers and the part is symmetric, so the part itself has no pin 1. Only the footprint sets the numbering.

Famicom numbering, from primary sources and confirmed three independent ways:
- NESdev (S3, current page, last edited 2026-08-31) says 'Pins 01-30 are on the label side of the cartridge, left to right'. In its diagram, 01-30 are the (front) column and 31 sits opposite 01.
- The OpenFC HVC-CPU-07 board file (S5) has slot pads 1-30 on the row toward the console front (the 15-pin expansion port). Pin 1 is at the left and 31 at the same X as 1.
- The NESdev figure of a measured Nintendo HVC-TGROM-01 cart (S4) has wide/long power pads at front positions 1, 16 and 30, and on the back only at the end behind pin 1. These are GND 1/16 and +5V 30/31.

Result: the label side carries 1-30. Looking at the label with the contacts down, pin 1 is the leftmost contact and 30 the rightmost. Pin 31 is directly behind 1 and 60 behind 30.

The J8 netlist matches the NESdev pinout on all 60 pins: 1/16 GND, 30/31 +5V_SW, 45 CART_AUD_OUT, 46 CART_AUD_RET. Symbol FC_CART60 pins '1'..'60' are the pad names.

Footprint convention:
- Origin at the centre of the hole array, which is also the centre of the body and of the slot. Rows run parallel to X.
- Pins 1-30 (label side) are on the row with the larger Y, Y=+2.54, with pin 1 at X=-36.83. Pins 31-60 are at Y=-2.54, and 31 has the same X as 1.
- Pads: drill 1.00 (JLCPCB finishes it at 0.92-1.13, inside the maker's 0.85-1.15). Pads Ø1.70 round, pin 1 a 1.70 square. That gives a 0.35 annular ring (0.285 at the largest hole) and a 0.84 copper and mask gap.
- F.SilkS: body outline, pin-1 triangle, corner numbers 1/30/31/60, and 'CART LABEL' on the +Y side.
- F.Fab: body with a chamfer at the pin-1/label corner, plus the slot.
- Courtyard: X +-41.75, Y +-6.85.

Recommended placement is rotation 0 at floorplan (110.0, 149.5). The label then faces the JAMMA edge, the CPU-bus pins sit at -X near U1 and the PPU-bus pins at +X near U6, as the floorplan zones expect. This keeps the current floorplan with three Pico 2 modules, in line with the decision to stay on Pico 2.

The 'other_geometry' field specifies a 1:1 check print with continuity tests: 1-16 and 30-31 must beep with the cartridge the right way round, and 45-60 must not. Nothing in the repository was edited and no .kicad_mod was written. Downloads are in /tmp/claude-0/fp-spec/cart60/.

spec.other_geometry:
ORIGIN AND AXES
- Origin (0,0) is the centre of the 2 x 30 hole array. It is also the centre of the body outline and of the card slot, because the maker's A/B/C/D chain and the section view are symmetric.
- X runs along the rows to the right; Y runs down (KiCad, top view).
- Row Y = +2.54 holds pins 1-30, the cartridge LABEL side. Row Y = -2.54 holds pins 31-60, the back.
- The card plane is Y = 0. The label face of a 1.2 mm Famicom card is at Y = +0.60.

PART DATA FOR FAB, CHECKS AND A 3D BOX (from S1)
- Body top outline 82.49 x 9.25: X +-41.245, Y +-4.625.
- Slot opening 79.04 x 2.00: X +-39.52, Y +-1.00, 9.00 deep.
- End legs: outer faces at X +-40.37; they are the seating plane.
- Lower base 7.50 wide (Y +-3.75). Upper part 10.20 tall. Total height 15.60 above the board.
- Tails 0.65 (X) x 0.40 (Y), 3.80 below the seating plane.
- No pegs, posts or NPTH.

F.Fab (line 0.10)
- Body as a closed polygon: (-41.245,-4.625) (41.245,-4.625) (41.245,4.625) (-40.245,4.625) (-41.245,3.625). This is the body with a 1.0 mm chamfer at the pin-1 / label corner, -X +Y.
- Slot rectangle (-39.52,-1.00) to (39.52,1.00).
- Text '${REFERENCE}' at (0,0): size 1.0, thickness 0.15.
- Property 'Value' 'Famicom_Cart_60' at (0,7.60): size 1.0, thickness 0.15.

F.SilkS (line 0.15 = JLCPCB minimum; text at least 1.0 high; every item is more than 1.3 from any pad, so the 0.15 pad-to-silk rule holds)
- Outline rectangle (-41.40,-4.78) to (41.40,4.78).
- Pin-1 marker: filled triangle (-36.83,5.00) (-37.48,6.10) (-36.18,6.10), apex pointing at pad 1.
- Numbers, size 1.0, thickness 0.15: '1' at (-38.60,5.70); '30' at (36.83,5.70); '31' at (-36.83,-5.70); '60' at (36.83,-5.70).
- 'CART LABEL' at (0,6.00), size 1.2, thickness 0.20. It means the cartridge label faces this (+Y) side. ASCII is used because KiCad's stroke font is safest for JLCPCB.
- Property 'Reference' at (0,-6.00), size 1.0, thickness 0.15.

F.CrtYd (line 0.05)
- Rectangle (-41.75,-6.85) to (41.75,6.85). This is the body + 0.5 in X. In Y it also covers the silk markings (max |Y| about 6.7), so DRC keeps parts from hiding the label marking. KLC's plain body + 0.5 would be Y +-5.13.

Dwgs.User (optional, line 0.10, for placement and the check print)
- Famicom card in the slot: (-39.20,-0.60) to (39.20,0.60), with text '1.2 mm cartridge PCB - label face +Y'.
- Provisional shell envelope from floorplan SHELL: (-54.0,-8.5) to (54.0,8.5), with text 'cart shell ~108x17 PROVISIONAL - measure'.
- The shell keepout and the guide-bracket NPTH holes (floorplan: X +-58.0, Y 0 from the origin) are board-level items, not part of this footprint.

ATTRIBUTES AND FIELDS
- attr through_hole.
- No paste layers (wave soldered).
- Datasheet field: https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C5173310
- Description field: 'WingTAT ED60BGFBK (LCSC C5173310) 60-way 2.54 mm card-edge slot, vertical THT, rows 5.08; Famicom numbering: 1-30 = cartridge label side (+Y), pin 1 at -X, 31 behind 1 (NESdev Cartridge connector)'.
- Tags: 'Famicom cartridge slot card edge 2x30 P2.54mm ED60BGFBK'.
- Thermal relief on the GND / +5V_SW pads (1, 16, 30, 31) comes from the zone defaults; do not set solid connection in the footprint.

BOARD PLACEMENT (not in the footprint)
- Origin at floorplan (110.00, 149.50), where floorplan y is measured up from the finger tips. That is 12.50 below the board's top edge, centred left-right.
- Rotation 0: the label row faces the JAMMA edge, and pin 1 is on the left in the normal top view.

1:1 CHECK PRINT (made by the stage-2 tools)
Make it from kicad-cli fp export svg (SVG in mm) plus a generated overlay. Print on A4 landscape at 100% / 'actual size': no fit-to-page, no mirroring.
1. Scale check.
   - A 100.00 mm bar and a 50.00 mm bar at right angles.
   - The dimension 'pad 1 centre to pad 30 centre = 73.66'.
   - Reprint if the bar is off by more than 0.5 mm.
   - The line 'TOP VIEW (parts side) - this text must read normally' catches a mirrored print.
2. Footprint top view at 1:1.
   - All 60 pads (Ø1.70, pad 1 square) with Ø1.00 drill dots, each numbered in characters at least 1.5 mm high.
   - The 82.49 x 9.25 body, the 79.04 x 2.00 slot, and the 78.4 x 1.2 card drawn inside the slot.
   - A large arrow and text on the +Y side: 'cartridge LABEL faces this way / カセットのラベル面'. Large 1 / 30 / 31 / 60 at the corners.
   - Pads 1 and 16 marked GND, pads 30 and 31 marked +5V.
   - An arrow 'toward the JAMMA fingers (board bottom edge)' showing the chosen rotation.
3. The two faces of the cartridge's card edge at 1:1, as seen holding the cartridge contacts-down.
   - Strip A, label face: 30 pads at 2.54 on a 78.4 wide edge, numbered 1..30 left to right. Pads 1 and 30 drawn 2.6 wide, pad 16 drawn 1 mm longer (the Nintendo pattern in the NESdev TGROM figure).
   - Strip B, back face (cartridge turned around): numbered 60..31 left to right, pad 31 at the right end drawn wide, with the note '31 is directly behind 1'.
   - The owner lays the contact edge on each strip. On Nintendo-made boards the wide and long contacts must coincide with the drawn ones; third-party boards may have uniform pads.
4. Multimeter table for the cartridge alone. Expected results:
   - Label-face contact 1 <-> label-face contact 16: beeps (both GND).
   - Label-face contact 30 <-> the back contact behind 1 (pin 31): beeps. +5V on both; NESdev notes cartridges link 30 and 31.
   - Label-face 1 <-> label-face 30: no beep.
5. Optional, with the LCSC sample from README chapter 8.
   - Lay the print on foam board and push the sample's 60 tails through the printed drill dots. All must land, which proves 2.54 / 5.08 / 73.66.
   - Insert the cartridge with its label toward the 'LABEL' side.
   - Probe the tails under the paper: printed 1 <-> printed 16 must beep; printed 30 <-> printed 31 must beep; printed 45 <-> printed 60 must NOT beep. A reversed cartridge gives 45-60 beep and 1-16 silent.
6. Title strip: footprint name, generator version or hash, date, and the sources (ED60BGFBK drawing Rev A; NESdev Cartridge connector 2026-08-31).
spec.kicad_syntax_notes:
The installed KiCad 10.0.8 library uses footprint format (version 20260206); write that (or run 'kicad-cli fp upgrade' on the generated library). Skeleton (uuid fields can be left out; KiCad adds them on load):

(footprint "Famicom_Cart_60" (version 20260206) (generator "fcgen") (layer "F.Cu")
  (descr "...") (tags "Famicom cartridge slot card edge 2x30 P2.54mm ED60BGFBK")
  (property "Reference" "REF**" (at 0 -6 0) (layer "F.SilkS") (effects (font (size 1 1) (thickness 0.15))))
  (property "Value" "Famicom_Cart_60" (at 0 7.6 0) (layer "F.Fab") (effects (font (size 1 1) (thickness 0.15))))
  (property "Datasheet" "https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C5173310" (at 0 0 0) (layer "F.Fab") (hide yes) (effects (font (size 1 1) (thickness 0.15))))
  (attr through_hole)
  (duplicate_pad_numbers_are_jumpers no)
  (fp_rect (start -41.4 -4.78) (end 41.4 4.78) (stroke (width 0.15) (type solid)) (fill no) (layer "F.SilkS"))
  (fp_poly (pts (xy -36.83 5) (xy -37.48 6.1) (xy -36.18 6.1)) (stroke (width 0.15) (type solid)) (fill yes) (layer "F.SilkS"))
  (fp_text user "CART LABEL" (at 0 6 0) (layer "F.SilkS") (effects (font (size 1.2 1.2) (thickness 0.2))))
  (fp_poly (pts (xy -41.245 -4.625) (xy 41.245 -4.625) (xy 41.245 4.625) (xy -40.245 4.625) (xy -41.245 3.625)) (stroke (width 0.1) (type solid)) (fill no) (layer "F.Fab"))
  (fp_rect (start -39.52 -1) (end 39.52 1) (stroke (width 0.1) (type solid)) (fill no) (layer "F.Fab"))
  (fp_text user "${REFERENCE}" (at 0 0 0) (layer "F.Fab") (effects (font (size 1 1) (thickness 0.15))))
  (fp_rect (start -41.75 -6.85) (end 41.75 6.85) (stroke (width 0.05) (type solid)) (fill no) (layer "F.CrtYd"))
  (pad "1" thru_hole rect (at -36.83 2.54) (size 1.7 1.7) (drill 1) (layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask") (remove_unused_layers no))
  (pad "2" thru_hole circle (at -34.29 2.54) (size 1.7 1.7) (drill 1) (layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask") (remove_unused_layers no))
  ... through pad "60" at (36.83 -2.54) ...)

Rules:
- Pad numbers are the strings "1".."60". They equal the FC_CART60 pin numbers; P1..P60 are symbol pin names only.
- No other numbered pads: the build checks that every symbol pin has a pad.
- Pad (at x y) is relative to the footprint origin, Y down.
- fp_rect and fp_poly take (fill no) or (fill yes), as in the installed library; property visibility is (hide yes).
- File: kicad/fcjamma.pretty/Famicom_Cart_60.kicad_mod, which fp-lib-table maps as fcjamma = ${KIPRJMOD}/fcjamma.pretty. Produce it with the generator, not by hand.

Checks the generator should assert:
- Pad 31 has the same X as pad 1, with Y 5.08 smaller.
- Pad 1 is at X < 0 and Y > 0.
- Pad 30 X minus pad 1 X = 73.66.
- Annular ring >= 0.25 at drill + 0.13.
- Pad-to-pad gap >= 0.13.
- The courtyard encloses the body + 0.5.

To load-check the file, use 'kicad-cli fp export svg --fp Famicom_Cart_60 kicad/fcjamma.pretty', or place it on a test board and run 'kicad-cli pcb drc'.
open_questions: Contact pressure and retention with 1.2 mm Famicom cards. The slot is built for 1.57 +-0.15 cards, with brass contacts, 1 µin gold flash and a 0.60 +-0.10 contact gap. Try the three LCSC samples with several cartridges before ordering (README chapters 7 #4 and 8).

Insertion depth against the shell. The contacts sit about 4.1 mm below the connector top (measured from the figure, not dimensioned), and Famicom signal pads start about 2.0 mm above the card's leading edge. So the card edge must stick out of the shell by at least about 6.6 mm, and it bottoms out at 9.0 mm. Measure how far it protrudes, and whether the shell rests on the 82.49 x 9.25 body top or straddles it.

Cartridge shell size and where the cart PCB sits within the shell thickness (centred or offset toward the label). These fix the keepout (now a provisional 108 x 17 centred box) and the guide-bracket NPTH holes (provisionally at X +-58.0, Y 0 from the J8 origin, 'not plated'; JLCPCB minimum NPTH 0.50).

The connector has no polarisation. A cartridge put in label-backwards puts its GND pins 1 and 16 on PD4 and CART_AUD_OUT while it still gets +5V_SW. Decide whether the guide bracket keys the shell, or whether the silkscreen alone is enough. Also decide whether Pico C firmware should check for a reversed cartridge, for example by reading the CIRAM lines, before a dump.

Final rotation. 0° (label toward the JAMMA edge) is recommended because the CPU and PPU sides then match the floorplan zones. Confirm the owner has no preference for which way the label faces in the cabinet.

Not dimensioned on the drawing: the end-leg footprint, the under-body gap (about 1.1 mm in the front view, absent in the section), and the body corner radii. The footprint uses a plain rectangle and keeps the courtyard free of other parts.

JLCPCB's process for this 60-pin part: wave with a pallet, selective, or by hand at 5 boards. Also whether the 2.2 mm tail protrusion is acceptable, and whether flux is kept out of the contacts. These are already asked in ordering/jlcpcb_support_question.txt item 2/2c; read the answer before stage 3.
Courtyard size. Y +-6.85 (covers the silk markings) was chosen over KLC's body + 0.5 (Y +-5.13). The footprint checker in task #23 should accept this, or the parent should pick one.

The 'front = label side' identification rests on NESdev's statement, the OpenFC front row and the TGROM 'Front' view. It has not yet been checked by continuity on a physical cartridge. The 1:1 print and multimeter steps above do that before ordering.

spec.summary:
I got the maker's drawing of the exact part: LCSC's datasheet for C118956, a BOCHEN 3362P approval sheet with the drawing on p.3. The datasheet link on the JLCPCB page returned AccessDenied. I compared it with the Bourns 3362 datasheet (REV. 03/25) and with LCSC's own EasyEDA footprint for C118956. All three agree on the pin pattern and on its handedness.

Frame: KiCad footprint frame, mm, X right, Y down, seen from the top. The origin is the centre of the pad bounding box, which is the same origin as LCSC/EasyEDA's footprint for this part, so JLCPCB's placement file lines up with their library.

Pads:
- Pad 1 at (-2.54, +1.27), pad 2 (wiper) at (0, -1.27), pad 3 at (+2.54, +1.27).
- Seen from the top with the marking edge ('1 3362 3' printed on the part) at +Y: pin 1 is on the left, pin 3 on the right, and pin 2 toward the far edge.
- BOCHEN rounds the spacing to 2.5. Bourns and LCSC's footprint use 2.54, and a 0.9 mm hole takes either.

Pins and holes:
- Pins are round. BOCHEN gives ø0.5; Bourns gives 0.46 ± 0.03.
- Neither maker recommends a hole size. I propose a 0.9 mm drill with 1.6 mm pads (annular ring 0.35). Pad 1 is a rounded rectangle, pads 2 and 3 are round.
- All of this is inside JLCPCB's limits: hole tolerance +0.13/-0.08, annular ring 0.25 recommended and 0.18 minimum, pad-to-silk 0.15, silk line 0.15.

Body:
- BOCHEN: 6.9 wide × 7.1 deep (including two small tabs on the marking edge) × 4.8 seated height (including 0.3 standoffs). Footprint y range is -2.23 to +4.87.
- Bourns: 6.60 × 6.99 × 4.88, each ±0.25.
- The adjusting screw is a cross-slot rotor on the top face, centred at (0, +0.97).

Pin functions:
- The circuit.py note ('pin 2 is the wiper; clockwise moves it towards pin 3, so clockwise is louder') is confirmed for the Bourns original. Its schematic reads '② WIPER', 'CCW ① … ③ CW', 'CLOCKWISE →'.
- The BOCHEN sheets (3362P, and its 3362S sibling) number the pins the same way but give no direction. For the fitted part the direction is likely the same but unverified, as circuit.py already says.
- With pin 1 on GND, pin 3 on AUD_SUM and the wiper on AMP_IN, turning clockwise is louder if clockwise runs toward pin 3. If it runs the other way, the only effect is a reversed volume direction.

Silkscreen, fab and courtyard:
- Silkscreen: a 0.15 mm body outline, a filled triangle at pin 1, and a clockwise arc arrow around the rotor above the far edge, with '+' at the clockwise (pin 3) end and '−' at the other end.
- Fab layer: the BOCHEN envelope, the rotor, and the part's printed pin-1 dot.
- Courtyard: (-3.70, -2.50) to (3.70, 5.15).

Height: the real height is at most 5.13 mm (Bourns 4.88 + 0.25; BOCHEN 4.8). floorplan.py's 7 mm is a safe overestimate. Its check() does not use height at all, only the oblique sketch does, and nothing tall is near RV1. Below the board the leads stick out at least 4.4 mm unless JLCPCB trims them.

Decision for you: before the boards are ordered, consider adding 5 × C118956 (about $0.87) to the planned LCSC sample order and checking the turning direction with an ohmmeter.

spec.summary: (a) SW3. Origin is the centre of pad 1, X runs across the two rows and Y runs along each row. The KiCad numbering already matches the HRO part. The maker numbers only the switches (1-4, printed on the cover opposite the 'ON' legend) and gives no terminal numbers. When the part is inserted with its 'ON' edge over the x=7.62 row and its '1' at the y=0 end, switch n joins pad n (x=0, I_DIPn, 10 k pull-up) to pad 9-n (x=7.62, GND). That gives ON (closed) = 0, as README 3.7 states. Changes: all 8 pads get a 1.0 mm drill and a 1.7 mm land. Pad 1 is a roundrect with rratio 0.147059 (r 0.25 mm); the others are circles. This gives a 0.35 mm annular ring (JLCPCB recommends at least 0.25; worst case is 0.21 against an absolute minimum of 0.18) and a 0.84 mm gap and solder mask web. Keeping the 1.6 mm land would leave a worst-case ring of 0.16 mm, which is too small. The maker recommends a Ø0.97±0.05 hole. The pin measures 0.60 × about 0.20 mm. New silkscreen, outside the body so it stays visible: 'ON' with an arrow on the +X side, and the numbers 1-4 beside pads 1-4. KiCad 10.0.8 DRC with JLCPCB-like rules reports 0 violations for this geometry. (b) U25-U27. Origin is the module centre; -Y points to the USB end. Pads 1-40, D1-D3, TP1-TP6 and the four USB-shell pads in the KiCad footprint match the Pico 2 datasheet Figure 5 exactly. Test-pad identities were confirmed from Raspberry Pi's own STEP silkscreen: TP2/USB_DM is at (+1.0, -24.3) and TP3/USB_DP at (-1.0, -24.3). TP7 (1V1) is at (+1.0, -5.0), so the README position is correct. The library already has a 1.9 mm rounded-square TP7 keep-out (TP7 + 0.2 mm, on F.Cu and F.Paste). Replace it with one rule area named 'TP7 keep-out' on F.Cu and F.Mask, a 2.5 mm circle (32-gon) that forbids tracks, vias, pads and pours. The mask stays closed because nothing on F.Mask can open there, and a board .kicad_dru rule enforces that. KiCad 10.0.8 DRC test result: a via, an F.Cu track and an F.Mask opening inside the area are all flagged. A B.Cu track is allowed. The GND pour stops at r ≈ 1.25 mm. Vias under the modules must be tented (README ch. 8). A footprint cannot express tenting; it is a board setting: (setup (tenting (front yes) (back yes))), no per-via 'Not tented' override, the JLCPCB 'Via Covering: Tented' order option, and a via drill of 0.4 mm or less. A tested DRC rule flags untented vias inside the module courtyards.

spec.kicad_syntax_notes:
1) A keep-out rule area inside a footprint, as KiCad 10 writes it (Module.pretty/RaspberryPi_Pico_SMD.kicad_mod, format 20260206), placed after the fp_* graphics and before (group)/(embedded_fonts)/(model):
(zone (layers "F.Cu" "F.Paste") (uuid "2c66c56a-...") (name "Pad Keep Out TP7") (hatch full 0.5) (connect_pads (clearance 0)) (min_thickness 0.25) (keepout (tracks not_allowed) (vias not_allowed) (pads not_allowed) (copperpour not_allowed) (footprints allowed)) (placement (enabled no) (sheetname "")) (fill (thermal_gap 0.5) (thermal_bridge_width 0.5) (island_removal_mode 0)) (polygon (pts (xy 0.052139 -5.515545) (xy 0.086068 -5.642167) ... (xy 0.05 -5.45))))
A single layer is written (layer "F.Cu"); several layers are written (layers "F.Cu" "F.Mask"). Of 475 library zones, 143 use (layer "F.Cu") and 60 use (layers "F.Cu" "F.Paste"). There is no 'rule_area' keyword: the (keepout ...) block makes the zone a rule area, and pcbnew reports GetIsRuleArea() == True. Zone outlines may contain arcs, e.g. RaspberryPi_Pico_Common_SMD: (pts (xy -0.6 22.9) (xy 0 22.9) (arc (start 0 26.5) (mid -0.707107 26.207107) (end -1 25.5)) (xy -1 23.3) ...). The tested 32-gon avoids arcs.
2) Proposed zone (tested in KiCad 10.0.8): (zone (layers "F.Cu" "F.Mask") (uuid "<stable>") (name "TP7 keep-out") (hatch full 0.5) (connect_pads (clearance 0)) (min_thickness 0.25) (keepout (tracks not_allowed) (vias not_allowed) (pads not_allowed) (copperpour not_allowed) (footprints allowed)) (placement (enabled no) (sheetname "")) (fill (thermal_gap 0.5) (thermal_bridge_width 0.5) (island_removal_mode 0)) (polygon (pts (xy 2.25 -5) (xy 2.225982 -4.756137) ... 32 points ...))).
3) Coordinate frames: in a .kicad_mod, zone points are relative to the footprint origin. When the same footprint sits in a .kicad_pcb, pcbnew stores its zones in ABSOLUTE board coordinates, while pads and fp_* graphics stay relative. Measured: a copy at (100,100) saved the TP7 zone as (xy 102.25 95) ..., and local points pasted into a board landed at the board origin. A tool that reads board files must allow for this.
4) tools/fcgen/footprint_out.Footprint.keepout() already writes this structure (hatch full 0.508, min_thickness 0.254, (layer)/(layers)), but it has no (name ...). Add a name argument, because the DRC rules refer to the area by name. With derive(), the edit function should remove find(tree, 'zone') from the copied tree before appending the new node; add_uuids() already assigns uuids to 'zone'.
5) DIP pads: (pad "1" thru_hole roundrect (at 0 0) (size 1.7 1.7) (drill 1) (layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask") (remove_unused_layers no) (roundrect_rratio 0.147059)); (pad "2" thru_hole circle (at 0 2.54) (size 1.7 1.7) (drill 1) (layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask") (remove_unused_layers no)); and so on. Silk text: (fp_text user "ON" (at 10.2 3.81 0) (layer "F.SilkS") (uuid ...) (effects (font (size 1 1) (thickness 0.15)))).
6) Via tenting cannot be expressed in a footprint; it is set on the board. (setup ... (tenting (front yes) (back yes)) (covering (front no) (back no)) (plugging (front no) (back no)) (capping no) (filling no) ...); per-via override (via (at x y) (size 0.6) (drill 0.3) (layers "F.Cu" "B.Cu") (tenting (front yes) (back yes)) (net "...") (uuid ...)). The pcbnew API has BOARD_DESIGN_SETTINGS.m_TentViasFront/m_TentViasBack and PCB_VIA.SetFrontTentingMode(pcbnew.TENTING_MODE_TENTED|NOT_TENTED|FROM_BOARD).
7) Board custom rules (fcjamma.kicad_dru), both tested with kicad-cli 10.0.8 'pcb drc':
(version 1)
(rule "TP7: solder mask stays closed" (layer "F.Mask") (condition "A.intersectsArea('TP7 keep-out')") (constraint disallow graphic text zone pad via))
(rule "Vias under a Pico are tented" (condition "A.Type == 'Via' && (A.intersectsCourtyard('U25') || A.intersectsCourtyard('U26') || A.intersectsCourtyard('U27')) && (A.Front_tenting == 'Not tented' || A.Back_tenting == 'Not tented')") (constraint disallow via))
The mask rule fires only when the rule area includes F.Mask. Keep-out violations are reported as type 'items_not_allowed'.
open_questions: Which terminal is pin 1 in JLCPCB's own (EasyEDA) footprint for C92645, the 'ON' row or the numbers row? The EasyEDA API answered 403 from this environment. At JLCPCB's placement check ($0.45, already in README ch. 8), confirm the part's printed '1' is at pads 1/8 and its 'ON' faces pads 5-8, the GND row marked 'ON →' on our silk.

Paste on D1-D3 (over-pasted 2.2 × 3.8), TP1-TP6 (1:1) and the USB-shell pads A-D (1:1) is KiCad's choice. Keep it, or ask JLCPCB in the pre-order question? Both library footprints use 0.12 mm silk lines, below JLCPCB's 0.15 mm legend minimum. Should the copies widen them?
